newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GWA sees export market strength.
newsitem.headline: GWA sees export market strength.

text.p: Home products company GWA International Ltd said on Wednesday it faced a difficult domestic market in 1995/96 and would continue to place increased emphasis on export sales in the current year.

The company said strong export sales and improved operating efficiencies allowed it to increase its final dividend by 12.5 percent to 4.5 cents, with the 1.6 percent fall in the 1995/96 net profit to A$30.12 million due to a higher tax rate.
"The further growth expected in export sales, improved operating performance and the release of new products should assist to offset the continued slow market conditions," it said.
Operating profit rose by 2.1 percent to A$48.3 million in the year to June 30.
Sales rose 9.5 percent to A$331.5 million and export sales rose 43.7 percent to A$50.3 million.
"Export performance was outstanding and assisted to offset the decline in the construction market which continued in the second half of the year," GWA chairman Barry Thornton said.
Thornton said the first half of the current year "would be a challenge with the current difficult market conditions expected to continue until the New Year".
